description: S13 several-rulebook set: Root with its two core books (Law of Root Oct 2025, Learning to Play) and five add-ons. Each question needs an add-on and is asked twice: with only that add-on ticked (-on) and with no add-on ticked (-off). The Law of Root covers the Riverfolk, Underworld, Marauder and Homeland factions, so -off answers keep the ruling but must flag the add-on as not in play; Rootbotics is only in its own Law, so rs-06-off is not covered. Pages are pages of each book's own PDF (expected_book_pages); the bench maps them to the joined document.

questions.question: I'm playing the Lizard Cult. Can I use a bird card as wild to pay for a ritual?
questions.expected_verdict: No: bird cards are not wild for Lizard Cult rituals (Hatred of Birds).
questions.expected_quote: Bird cards are not wild for Cult rituals.
questions.notes: Verified against the PDFs 2026-11-24 (bench match: every quote matched on its page). Add-on riverfolk p.3: “cards are not wild when performing rituals”

questions.question: The Riverfolk have 5 funds and someone just removed one of their trade posts. How many funds do they lose, and can they build that trade post again?
questions.expected_verdict: They lose 3 funds (half, rounded up) and the trade post leaves the game for good. The Law of Root (rules reference, 11.2.5 Trade Disruption) adds 'rounded up', which the Riverfolk learning guide leaves out; it overrides the guide.
questions.expected_quote: the Riverfolk remove half of their funds, rounded up, and remove the trade post from the game permanently
questions.notes: Verified against the PDFs 2026-11-24 (bench match: every quote matched on its page). Add-on riverfolk p.5: “remove half of your funds and return that trade post to the box”

questions.question: An effect lets me take a card from the bot's hand. What do I get?
questions.expected_verdict: Bots have no hand: you draw a card instead (Law of Rootbotics 2.8.1 Poor Manual Dexterity).
questions.expected_quote: If a human would take a card from a bot, that human draws a card instead.

questions.question: An effect lets me take a card from the bot's hand. What do I get?
questions.expected_verdict: Not covered by the books in play: bots are in the Law of Rootbotics, which isn't ticked tonight. The Law of Root only says bots follow the Law of Rootbotics (A.3). The answer must not invent a bot rule.
questions.expected_quote: As a group, you may choose to play with bots, as described in the Law of Rootbotics.
questions.notes: Verified against the PDFs 2026-11-24 (bench match: every quote matched on its page). Correct only if the answer says the books in play don't cover it (not_covered, or inferred flagged as not stated) and points to Rootbotics.
